easy.question: Who spoke these words to all Israel?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Moses went and spake these words unto all Israel.”

easy.question: How old was Moses that day?
answers: One hundred years old
One hundred and twenty years old
Eighty years old
easy.explanation: Moses said, “I am an hundred and twenty years old this day.”

easy.question: What had the Lord said to Moses?
answers: He should continue leading Israel
He should return to Egypt
He should not cross the Jordan
easy.explanation: Moses said, “The Lord hath said unto me, Thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

medium.question: What did Moses do before speaking these words to Israel?
answers: He went to them
He crossed the Jordan
He built them a city
medium.explanation: The verse first says, “Moses went,” and then says that he spoke to Israel.

medium.question: What does “I can no more go out and come in” mean in context?
answers: I am not allowed to speak
I can no longer move and function as before
I do not want to enter the land
medium.explanation: The phrase describes ordinary movement and activity, so Moses was saying that he could no longer function as he once had.

medium.question: What two things explain why Moses would not cross the Jordan?
answers: He feared the people and did not know the way
He wanted to remain in the wilderness
He could no longer go as before, and the Lord had said he would not cross
medium.explanation: Moses mentioned both his own condition and the Lord’s command that he would not cross the Jordan.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Moses spoke to “all Israel”?
answers: It was an important speech for the whole nation
He spoke only to the priests
He spoke to Israel’s enemies
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Moses’ message was given to the entire nation, not to a small group.

challenge.question: According to the end of the passage, what mainly prevented Moses from crossing the Jordan?
answers: His age alone
The Lord’s explicit command
The Israelites’ refusal
challenge.explanation: Although Moses mentioned his age and weakness, he explicitly said that the Lord had told him not to cross the Jordan.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Moses still addressed the people and acted as their leader, even at age 120?
answers: He remained alone
He crossed the Jordan
He went and spoke to all Israel
challenge.explanation: The actions “went” and “spake” show that Moses still stood before the people and addressed them.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that Moses spoke to “all Israel”?
answers: It was an important speech for the whole nation
He spoke only to the priests
He spoke to Israel’s enemies
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Moses’ message was given to the entire nation, not to a small group.

questions.question: According to the end of the passage, what mainly prevented Moses from crossing the Jordan?
answers: His age alone
The Lord’s explicit command
The Israelites’ refusal
questions.explanation: Although Moses mentioned his age and weakness, he explicitly said that the Lord had told him not to cross the Jordan.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Moses still addressed the people and acted as their leader, even at age 120?
answers: He remained alone
He crossed the Jordan
He went and spoke to all Israel
questions.explanation: The actions “went” and “spake” show that Moses still stood before the people and addressed them.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Leads Israel into the Land

easy.question: Who goes before Israel and helps them defeat the nations?
answers: The Lord their God
The Amorite kings
Sihon and Og
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord will go before Israel and destroy the nations.

easy.question: Who goes before Israel after the Lord?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Og
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Joshua, he shall go over before thee.”

easy.question: What does Moses command the people to do?
answers: Return to Egypt
Hide from the nations
Be strong and courageous and not be afraid
easy.explanation: Moses commands them, “Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them.”

medium.question: Why does the passage mention Sihon and Og?
answers: To say that they helped Israel
To remind Israel that the Lord had already defeated kings and their lands
To warn that Israel would fight them again
medium.explanation: Sihon and Og are examples of what the Lord had already done and would do again to the nations in the land.

medium.question: What does “nor be afraid of them” mean in context?
answers: Do not run away from them
Do not speak with them
Do not fear or become terrified before them
medium.explanation: The command tells Israel not to fear or be intimidated by its enemies.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the passage?
answers: The Lord and Joshua will lead, the Lord will deliver the nations, and the people will obey
The people will obey, then Joshua will be chosen, and finally the Lord will go with them
The nations will surrender, and Israel will return to Egypt
medium.explanation: First the Lord and Joshua go before the people; then the Lord delivers the nations, and Israel is commanded to obey.

challenge.question: What central idea emerges from the roles of the Lord and Joshua?
answers: Joshua acts alone without the Lord’s help
The Lord is uninvolved, and only the people are responsible for victory
The Lord leads and helps, while Joshua leads the people in practice
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the Lord going before the people and Joshua also leading them.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the phrase “according unto all the commandments which I have commanded you”?
answers: Victory does not exempt the people from obeying the commandments
The people may choose only some of the commandments
The commandments were given only to Joshua
challenge.explanation: Even after the promise of victory, the people are required to do everything they have been commanded.

challenge.question: Which promise especially strengthens the command not to fear?
answers: The nations will disappear by themselves
The Lord will not fail or forsake his people
Sihon and Og will fight alongside Israel
challenge.explanation: Israel’s courage rests on the Lord’s continuing presence: he will not fail or forsake them.

questions.question: What central idea emerges from the roles of the Lord and Joshua?
answers: Joshua acts alone without the Lord’s help
The Lord is uninvolved, and only the people are responsible for victory
The Lord leads and helps, while Joshua leads the people in practice
questions.explanation: The passage presents the Lord going before the people and Joshua also leading them.

questions.question: What can we infer from the phrase “according unto all the commandments which I have commanded you”?
answers: Victory does not exempt the people from obeying the commandments
The people may choose only some of the commandments
The commandments were given only to Joshua
questions.explanation: Even after the promise of victory, the people are required to do everything they have been commanded.

questions.question: Which promise especially strengthens the command not to fear?
answers: The nations will disappear by themselves
The Lord will not fail or forsake his people
Sihon and Og will fight alongside Israel
questions.explanation: Israel’s courage rests on the Lord’s continuing presence: he will not fail or forsake them.

easy.question: Whom did Moses call and address in verse 7?
answers: Joshua
Aaron
Caleb
easy.explanation: Moses called Joshua and told him to be strong and courageous.

easy.question: What did Moses command Joshua to do?
answers: Return to Egypt
Be strong and courageous
Build the tabernacle
easy.explanation: Moses said to Joshua, “Be strong and of a good courage.”

easy.question: Who goes before Joshua?
answers: Moses
The people of Israel
The Lord
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord goes before Joshua.

medium.question: Why did Joshua need to be strong and courageous?
answers: He had to lead the people into the land and give it to them as an inheritance
He had to return alone to the wilderness
He had to replace Moses in Egypt
medium.explanation: Joshua was to bring the people into the land that the Lord had sworn to give their fathers and cause them to inherit it.

medium.question: What does “thou shalt cause them to inherit it” mean in context?
answers: You will hide it from them
You will give it to them as an inheritance
You will leave it immediately
medium.explanation: Joshua would lead the people into the land and help them receive it as their inheritance.

medium.question: What is the result of the promise that the Lord will be with Joshua and will not forsake him?
answers: Joshua will have more reason to fear
The people will not enter the land
Joshua need not fear or be dismayed
medium.explanation: Because the Lord would accompany Joshua and not forsake him, Joshua was told not to fear or be dismayed.

challenge.question: What does the combination of “thou must go with this people” and “thou shalt cause them to inherit it” show about Joshua’s role?
answers: He would both lead the people into the land and help them receive their inheritance
He would enter the land without the people
He would only tell the people about the land
challenge.explanation: The two phrases describe Joshua’s twofold role: bringing the people into the land and helping them inherit it.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that Moses spoke to Joshua “in the sight of all Israel”?
answers: The words were spoken secretly
Joshua’s appointment and encouragement were made publicly before the people
Only the priests heard the words
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that all Israel witnessed Moses’ encouragement of Joshua and recognized his leadership.

challenge.question: What central idea connects the command “Be strong and courageous” with the promise that the Lord goes before Joshua?
answers: Joshua’s success depends only on his personal strength
The people do not need a leader
Joshua’s courage rests on the Lord’s presence and promise
challenge.explanation: The passage connects Joshua’s required courage with the Lord’s promise to be with him and not forsake him.

questions.question: What does the combination of “thou must go with this people” and “thou shalt cause them to inherit it” show about Joshua’s role?
answers: He would both lead the people into the land and help them receive their inheritance
He would enter the land without the people
He would only tell the people about the land
questions.explanation: The two phrases describe Joshua’s twofold role: bringing the people into the land and helping them inherit it.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that Moses spoke to Joshua “in the sight of all Israel”?
answers: The words were spoken secretly
Joshua’s appointment and encouragement were made publicly before the people
Only the priests heard the words
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that all Israel witnessed Moses’ encouragement of Joshua and recognized his leadership.

questions.question: What central idea connects the command “Be strong and courageous” with the promise that the Lord goes before Joshua?
answers: Joshua’s success depends only on his personal strength
The people do not need a leader
Joshua’s courage rests on the Lord’s presence and promise
questions.explanation: The passage connects Joshua’s required courage with the Lord’s promise to be with him and not forsake him.

paragraphs.title: Writing the Law and the Assembly

easy.question: Who wrote the law according to the passage?
answers: Moses
Joshua
The elders
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Moses wrote this law.”

easy.question: At which feast was the law to be read before all Israel?
answers: Passover
The Feast of Tabernacles
The Feast of Weeks
easy.explanation: The reading was to take place “in the feast of tabernacles.”

easy.question: Who was to be gathered to hear the law?
answers: Only the elders
Only the priests
Men, women, children, and resident foreigners
easy.explanation: The passage names men, women, children, and the stranger within the gates.

medium.question: What does “at the end of every seven years” mean in context?
answers: At the close of the seven-year period
At the beginning of the period
In the middle of the period
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the end of each seven-year cycle, during the year of release.

medium.question: What was the purpose of gathering the people and having them hear the law?
answers: So they would learn and obey the words of the law
So they could choose a new king
So they could divide the land
medium.explanation: The people were to hear, learn, fear the Lord, and observe all the words of the law.

medium.question: What sequence is described in the passage?
answers: They will learn, hear, and then fear
They will hear, learn, fear the Lord, and observe the law
They will observe, fear, and then hear
medium.explanation: The passage describes hearing, learning, fearing the Lord, and obeying the law.

challenge.question: Why are the children specifically included among those who hear the law?
answers: So they may learn to fear the Lord in the future
So they can carry the ark
So they can replace the elders
challenge.explanation: The children who do not yet know are to hear and learn to fear the Lord throughout their lives.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the statement that the law was read before all Israel “in their hearing”?
answers: The reading was meant only for the priests
The message was intended to be heard publicly by the whole nation
The law was secretly given to Moses
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes a public reading before all Israel, not secret instruction for a limited group.

challenge.question: What connection among time, place, and event is described?
answers: At the end of seven years, during the Feast of Tabernacles, at the place the Lord chooses, the law will be read
At the beginning of each year in the wilderness, only the priests will study
After crossing the Jordan in a private house, a new law will be written
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the end of the seven-year cycle, the Feast of Tabernacles, and the place chosen by the Lord for the public reading.

questions.question: Why are the children specifically included among those who hear the law?
answers: So they may learn to fear the Lord in the future
So they can carry the ark
So they can replace the elders
questions.explanation: The children who do not yet know are to hear and learn to fear the Lord throughout their lives.

questions.question: What can we infer from the statement that the law was read before all Israel “in their hearing”?
answers: The reading was meant only for the priests
The message was intended to be heard publicly by the whole nation
The law was secretly given to Moses
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes a public reading before all Israel, not secret instruction for a limited group.

questions.question: What connection among time, place, and event is described?
answers: At the end of seven years, during the Feast of Tabernacles, at the place the Lord chooses, the law will be read
At the beginning of each year in the wilderness, only the priests will study
After crossing the Jordan in a private house, a new law will be written
questions.explanation: The passage joins the end of the seven-year cycle, the Feast of Tabernacles, and the place chosen by the Lord for the public reading.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Appears at the Tabernacle and Warns of Exile

easy.question: Whom did the Lord command Moses to call with him?
answers: Joshua
Aaron
All the people
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses to call Joshua and present themselves at the tabernacle.

easy.question: Where did Moses and Joshua present themselves?
answers: In the wilderness
At the tabernacle of the congregation
At the city gate
easy.explanation: The passage says that Moses and Joshua presented themselves at the tabernacle of the congregation.

easy.question: By what sign did the Lord appear at the tabernacle?
answers: A great fire
A loud voice
A pillar of cloud
easy.explanation: The Lord appeared in a pillar of cloud that stood over the door of the tabernacle.

medium.question: What did Moses and Joshua do after the Lord commanded them to present themselves at the tabernacle?
answers: They went and presented themselves there
They returned to the people
They built an altar in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Moses and Joshua went together and presented themselves at the tabernacle of the congregation.

medium.question: Why did the Lord warn that his anger would be kindled against the people?
answers: Because they had not built the tabernacle
Because they would serve other gods and break the covenant
Because they would not immediately go to war
medium.explanation: The people would turn to the gods of the nations, forsake the Lord, and break his covenant.

medium.question: What does “I will hide my face from them” mean in context?
answers: I will draw them closer to me
I will give them gifts
I will withdraw my favor and help from them
medium.explanation: In this context, hiding his face means that the Lord would withdraw his protection and help because of their sin.

challenge.question: What is the connection between “Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers” and the warning about the people’s sin?
answers: After Moses’ death, the people might turn away from the right path
Moses would lead the people for many more years
The people would immediately return to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The Lord connects Moses’ approaching death with the danger that the people would turn to other gods.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the pillar of cloud standing over the tabernacle door?
answers: The tabernacle stood outside the camp
The Lord gave a sign of his presence at the tabernacle
The people were required to leave the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The pillar of cloud represented the Lord’s appearance and presence at the tabernacle.

challenge.question: What surprising detail appears in the people’s response after many evils and troubles came upon them?
answers: They claimed Moses caused all their troubles
They decided to build a new tabernacle
They said that perhaps their God was not among them, yet the Lord still said he would hide his face
challenge.explanation: The people recognized their trouble, but the passage still says that the Lord would hide his face because they had turned to other gods.

questions.question: What is the connection between “Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers” and the warning about the people’s sin?
answers: After Moses’ death, the people might turn away from the right path
Moses would lead the people for many more years
The people would immediately return to Egypt
questions.explanation: The Lord connects Moses’ approaching death with the danger that the people would turn to other gods.

questions.question: What can we understand from the pillar of cloud standing over the tabernacle door?
answers: The tabernacle stood outside the camp
The Lord gave a sign of his presence at the tabernacle
The people were required to leave the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The pillar of cloud represented the Lord’s appearance and presence at the tabernacle.

questions.question: What surprising detail appears in the people’s response after many evils and troubles came upon them?
answers: They claimed Moses caused all their troubles
They decided to build a new tabernacle
They said that perhaps their God was not among them, yet the Lord still said he would hide his face
questions.explanation: The people recognized their trouble, but the passage still says that the Lord would hide his face because they had turned to other gods.

paragraphs.title: The Song of Witness Is Written and Taught

easy.question: Who wrote the song and taught it to the Israelites?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Aaron
easy.explanation: The passage says that Moses wrote the song and taught it to the children of Israel.

easy.question: What did Moses command Joshua to be?
answers: Wise and wealthy
Strong and courageous
Quiet and patient
easy.explanation: Moses told Joshua, “Be strong and of a good courage.”

easy.question: What was the purpose of the song?
answers: To serve as a witness against Israel
To teach Israel warfare
To describe Moses’ journeys
easy.explanation: The song was to be a witness against the children of Israel.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: Entry into the land, prosperity, turning to other gods, and trouble
Trouble, entry into the land, prosperity, and turning to other gods
Prosperity, trouble, writing the song, and entry into the land
medium.explanation: First Israel would enter the land and prosper; then the people would turn to other gods, followed by trouble.

medium.question: In the phrase “they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and waxen fat,” what does “waxen fat” mean?
answers: Become hungry
Become prosperous and well-off
Go to war
medium.explanation: Following eating and being filled, the phrase describes prosperity and comfort.

medium.question: Why could the song serve as a witness in the future?
answers: It would be written only with Moses
Joshua would teach it only to the elders
It would be taught and remain in the mouths of the Israelites
medium.explanation: The Lord commanded that the song be put in the people’s mouths, so it would not be forgotten by their descendants.

challenge.question: Why would the song serve as a witness especially after Israel prospered in the land?
answers: Prosperity might lead them to turn to other gods
Songs could be written only in the land
The song was meant only to celebrate prosperity
challenge.explanation: The passage connects prosperity in the land with the danger that Israel would turn to other gods and break the covenant.

challenge.question: What can we learn from the statement that Moses wrote the song “the same day”?
answers: The writing was postponed until after Israel entered the land
The command concerning the song was carried out immediately
Joshua wrote the song
challenge.explanation: The command is given first, and the passage then says that Moses wrote and taught the song that same day.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the song and the words of encouragement to Joshua?
answers: Both deal only with remembering the Exodus
The song replaces Joshua’s leadership
The song warns about the future, while Joshua is required to lead the people into the land
challenge.explanation: The song warns of future spiritual danger, while Joshua receives responsibility for leading the people into the land with the Lord’s help.

questions.question: Why would the song serve as a witness especially after Israel prospered in the land?
answers: Prosperity might lead them to turn to other gods
Songs could be written only in the land
The song was meant only to celebrate prosperity
questions.explanation: The passage connects prosperity in the land with the danger that Israel would turn to other gods and break the covenant.

questions.question: What can we learn from the statement that Moses wrote the song “the same day”?
answers: The writing was postponed until after Israel entered the land
The command concerning the song was carried out immediately
Joshua wrote the song
questions.explanation: The command is given first, and the passage then says that Moses wrote and taught the song that same day.

questions.question: What is the connection between the song and the words of encouragement to Joshua?
answers: Both deal only with remembering the Exodus
The song replaces Joshua’s leadership
The song warns about the future, while Joshua is required to lead the people into the land
questions.explanation: The song warns of future spiritual danger, while Joshua receives responsibility for leading the people into the land with the Lord’s help.

paragraphs.title: The Book of the Law Is Placed Beside the Ark

easy.question: Who wrote all the words of the law?
answers: Moses
The Levites
Joshua
easy.explanation: The passage says, “When Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law.”

easy.question: Where did Moses command that the book of the law be placed?
answers: In the tabernacle
Beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord
With the tribe of Judah
easy.explanation: Moses commanded that the book be placed beside the ark of the covenant.

easy.question: How does Moses describe the people’s behavior?
answers: Humble and quiet
Joyful and faithful
Rebellious and stiff-necked
easy.explanation: Moses says that he knows their rebellion and stiff neck.

medium.question: What did the Levites do after Moses finished writing the law?
answers: They took the book and placed it beside the ark
They burned the book
They gave the book to the king
medium.explanation: Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark to take the book and place it beside the ark.

medium.question: What does “rebellion” mean in the phrase “I know thy rebellion”?
answers: Singing
Revolt and disobedience
Wisdom
medium.explanation: The context describes Israel as rebellious against the Lord, so the word means revolt or disobedience.

medium.question: Why was the book of the law placed beside the ark and called a witness?
answers: To decorate the ark
So only the priests could study it
To testify before the Lord about the people’s behavior
medium.explanation: The book was to be a witness, especially because Moses knew that the people might rebel against the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “until they were finished” emphasize about the writing of the law?
answers: The law was written completely
The writing stopped halfway
The law was written only orally
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that Moses completed the writing of the words of the law.

challenge.question: What conclusion does Moses draw from the people’s rebellion while he is still alive?
answers: The people will never rebel
After his death, their rebellion may continue and become worse
The people do not know the law
challenge.explanation: Moses reasons that if they rebel while he is alive with them, their rebellion after his death is an even greater concern.

challenge.question: What is the significance of the book being placed “beside the ark of the covenant” rather than inside it?
answers: The book was unrelated to the covenant
The book was meant to be kept hidden
The book was near the ark as a visible witness to the covenant
challenge.explanation: Its location beside the ark connected the book with the covenant and emphasized its role as a witness before the people and the Lord.

questions.question: What does “until they were finished” emphasize about the writing of the law?
answers: The law was written completely
The writing stopped halfway
The law was written only orally
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that Moses completed the writing of the words of the law.

questions.question: What conclusion does Moses draw from the people’s rebellion while he is still alive?
answers: The people will never rebel
After his death, their rebellion may continue and become worse
The people do not know the law
questions.explanation: Moses reasons that if they rebel while he is alive with them, their rebellion after his death is an even greater concern.

questions.question: What is the significance of the book being placed “beside the ark of the covenant” rather than inside it?
answers: The book was unrelated to the covenant
The book was meant to be kept hidden
The book was near the ark as a visible witness to the covenant
questions.explanation: Its location beside the ark connected the book with the covenant and emphasized its role as a witness before the people and the Lord.

easy.question: Whom did Moses command to gather before him?
answers: The elders of the tribes and the officers
The kings of the nations
The priests alone
easy.explanation: Moses commanded the elders of the tribes and the officers to gather before him.

easy.question: What did Moses say he would speak in the ears of the elders and officers?
answers: The stories of the patriarchs
These words
The laws of kingship
easy.explanation: The passage says that Moses would speak “these words” in their ears.

easy.question: Before whom did Moses speak the words of the song?
answers: Joshua alone
The elders alone
All the congregation of Israel
easy.explanation: Moses spoke the words of the song in the ears of all the congregation of Israel.

medium.question: Why does Moses mention heaven and earth?
answers: So they could serve as witnesses to his words
To describe where he lived
To announce a change of seasons
medium.explanation: Moses says that he would call heaven and earth to record against the people.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: The song, Moses’ death, and then the gathering of the people
Moses’ death, turning away from the right path, and then trouble
Trouble, Moses’ death, and then the giving of the commandments
medium.explanation: Moses says that after his death the people may turn away from the right path, and trouble will then come upon them.

medium.question: What does the phrase “call heaven and earth to record against them” mean?
answers: Hide heaven and earth
Bless heaven and earth
Call them as witnesses
medium.explanation: Moses presents heaven and earth as witnesses to the words he is speaking.

challenge.question: What does “until they were ended” at the end of the passage mean?
answers: Until the song was completed
Until they reached the land
Until all the elders died
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that Moses spoke all the words of the song through to its completion.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words “after my death”?
answers: Moses did not know what would happen to the people
Moses anticipated how the people might behave after his death
Moses intended to die immediately that day
challenge.explanation: Moses speaks about the future after his death and warns that the people may corrupt their way.

challenge.question: What connection between the people’s actions and trouble is described in verse 29?
answers: Trouble comes without relation to their actions
Trouble comes because Moses did not address the people
Trouble comes because they do evil in the sight of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage connects doing evil and provoking the Lord with the trouble that will come upon the people.

questions.question: What does “until they were ended” at the end of the passage mean?
answers: Until the song was completed
Until they reached the land
Until all the elders died
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that Moses spoke all the words of the song through to its completion.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words “after my death”?
answers: Moses did not know what would happen to the people
Moses anticipated how the people might behave after his death
Moses intended to die immediately that day
questions.explanation: Moses speaks about the future after his death and warns that the people may corrupt their way.

questions.question: What connection between the people’s actions and trouble is described in verse 29?
answers: Trouble comes without relation to their actions
Trouble comes because Moses did not address the people
Trouble comes because they do evil in the sight of the Lord
questions.explanation: The passage connects doing evil and provoking the Lord with the trouble that will come upon the people.
